company_items.summary: AutoZone beat FQ4 EPS estimates with $56.05 vs. the Street's $54.03, but the beat was low quality — driven by a 145 basis point tariff refund tailwind and a 105 basis point non-cash LIFO benefit to gross margins. Domestic comps missed badly at +1.6% vs. the Street's +3.1%, and the operating expense ratio worsened 100 basis points year-over-year. Management noted improving sales linearity in the final 8 weeks of the quarter and expressed confidence heading into fiscal 2027.

Cognex announced the acquisition of RealSense, the market leader in depth-sensing cameras and vision technology for robotic perception and Physical AI, for approximately $500 million upfront plus an additional ~$106.5 million. RealSense is expected to generate $80–90 million in revenue, representing more than 50% year-over-year growth. The deal positions Cognex at the intersection of robotics and AI-driven machine vision.

MillerKnoll delivered solid FQ1 EPS upside at 53 cents vs. the Street's 36 cents, and notably would have beaten even excluding the 11-cent tariff refund tailwind (adjusted EPS of 42 cents still topped consensus). Sales missed, falling 3.3% organically to $923.4 million vs. the $943.2 million estimate, though orders rose 3.5% year-over-year. Full-year fiscal 2027 sales guidance was trimmed modestly while EPS guidance was left unchanged, and FQ2 EPS guidance midpoint is in line with consensus.

Pentair named Bob Hau as its new CFO, effective November 1, with current interim CFO Bob Fishman staying on through that date to ensure a smooth transition. Hau brings extensive experience, having previously served as CFO at Fiserv, TE Connectivity, and Lennox International.

THOR Industries missed FQ4 EPS estimates with 78 cents vs. the Street's 87 cents, as gross margins fell 230 basis points year-over-year to 12.4% against a 13.85% estimate, and management cited stubborn interest rates, elevated fuel costs, and inflationary pressures weighing on retail demand. Revenue came in at $2.311 billion, down 8.4%, though it slightly topped the $2.17 billion estimate. Bright spots included healthy dealer inventory levels, structural cost-reduction actions, and a roughly 75% year-over-year surge in the North American towable RV order backlog.

Viking Therapeutics shares spiked in pre-market trading after reporting positive trial results for its GLP-1 drug VK2735, including an impressive 22% weight loss outcome. The strong data reinforces Viking's competitive positioning in the increasingly crowded but high-value obesity drug market.

tts_summary:
Good morning. This is a company-specific earnings note for Tuesday, September 22nd, with six names reporting before the open. Let's go through them.

Starting with AutoZone. The company beat fourth quarter earnings per share estimates — fifty-six oh five versus the Street at fifty-four oh three — but do not get too excited about this one. The beat was low quality. It was propped up by tariff refunds, which added 145 basis points to gross margins, and a non-cash LIFO adjustment worth another 105 basis points. Strip those out and the story gets worse fast. Domestic comps came in at plus 1.6% against a Street estimate of plus 3.1% — a meaningful miss — and the operating expense ratio worsened 100 basis points year-over-year. Management did note improving sales momentum in the final eight weeks of the quarter and said they feel well positioned heading into fiscal 2027, but the core results here were underwhelming.

Next, Cognex is acquiring RealSense — the market leader in depth-sensing cameras and vision technology for robotics and physical AI — for roughly five hundred million dollars upfront plus an additional hundred and six and a half million. RealSense is expected to deliver eighty to ninety million dollars in revenue, growing more than fifty percent year-over-year. This is a strategic move squarely into the robotics and AI perception space and is bullish for Cognex.

MillerKnoll beat first quarter EPS solidly — fifty-three cents versus thirty-six cents expected — and crucially, the beat holds up even after backing out an eleven-cent tariff refund tailwind. So adjusted earnings of forty-two cents still topped consensus. Sales missed at nine twenty-three versus the Street's nine forty-three, though orders were up 3.5% year-over-year. Full-year sales guidance was trimmed slightly, but EPS guidance was left unchanged. Second quarter EPS guidance midpoint is roughly in line with consensus. Call this mixed but leaning constructive.

Pentair named Bob Hau as its next CFO, effective November first. Hau previously held the CFO role at Fiserv, TE Connectivity, and Lennox. This is a routine management transition — not a meaningful market mover.

THOR Industries missed on fourth quarter earnings — seventy-eight cents versus eighty-seven cents expected. Gross margins fell 230 basis points year-over-year to 12.4%, well below the nearly 14% the Street was modeling. Management's tone was cautious, citing stubborn interest rates, high fuel costs, and inflation squeezing consumer budgets. The company is not providing formal fiscal 2027 guidance until later in the fall. That said, there were pockets of optimism — dealer inventory is at healthy levels, structural cost actions are underway, and the North American towable RV order backlog surged roughly 75% year-over-year. Still, this is a bearish print overall.

Finally, Viking Therapeutics is spiking pre-market on positive clinical trial data for VK2735, its GLP-1 obesity drug. The headline number — 22% weight loss — is strong and reinforces Viking's standing as a credible competitor in the obesity drug race. This is a clear bullish catalyst.

Bottom line for today: the macro backdrop and broader index context are not covered in this note — it's purely company-specific. Key names to watch are Viking to the upside and THOR to the downside. AutoZone's quality of beat will likely draw scrutiny on the open.
